Gem Diamonds averaged $1,395 a carat in the first half of 2026, up 38% from $1,008 a year earlier, and eight seven-figure stones did outsized work getting it there.

The Letseng producer sold 42,624 carats for $59.5 million, per its 28 July trading update. Those eight stones over $1 million brought $16.1 million alone, more than a quarter of the half's revenue, led by a 52.24-carat white at $32,908 a carat.

The average hides a swing: this desk's own arithmetic puts Q1 at $1,878 a carat against an implied $1,073 in Q2. And De Beers' own H1 realised rough price, $105 a carat, is the reminder this is an exceptional-stone story, not the broader rough market.

Gold was written back to the tape at $4,643.90 an ounce this morning, the highest mark this series has carried since it opened on 5 August at $4,158.30.

Kitco's 05:58 ET reading is up $41.50, or 0.90%, on Friday's close, and TradingEconomics corroborated it within 0.065% the same hour. Silver eased to $68.74, down 0.17%. Platinum and palladium both stay held at $1,881.00 and $1,336.00, a third straight session, after Kitco and TradingEconomics again split by more than a point.

Gold is the number every desk will print. The two held marks are the ones worth watching for when they finally move.
